issue.description:
Fix the known defect in the serve signal path: the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers do not set the shutdown flag. Depends on serve dispatch existing.

Acceptance criteria:
- SIGINT/SIGTERM set observable shutdown state (PoolManager shutdown flag / signal self-pipe) so the accept/poll loop stops promptly, bounded by ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS.
- On shutdown the daemon reaps every child worker, closes descriptors, and removes only the daemon-owned socket path, then exits cleanly.
- No worker respawn after shutdown is requested (maintain() guard holds under signal shutdown).
issue.notes:
Outcome: the named defect does not exist in committed main — the SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown path was already repaired by the serve-dispatch bead's commit 8454cbc, and every acceptance criterion holds. No file changes needed; verification-only close.

What the committed code does (src/pool.rs):
- install_serve_signal_handlers() installs serve_signal_handler for SIGINT+SIGTERM; the handler stores true into the SERVE_SIGNALED static AtomicBool (the only async-signal-safe thing it can touch).
- accept_loop relays SERVE_SIGNALED into PoolManager::shutdown() on every tick, then breaks when the manager flag is set. The poll(2) wake is immediate on EINTR and the flag check is bounded by ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS (250ms) even when the signal lands on a warmup thread.
- After run() returns, run_serve calls manager.shutdown_all() (SIGTERM -> bounded WNOHANG reap loop -> SIGKILL -> blocking waitpid per worker; closes each PTY master fd; drops each hook installer) then server.cleanup() removes exactly the bound socket path, then exit 0.
- maintain() early-returns on the shutdown flag, and accept_loop checks the flag before the maintain tick, so no respawn after shutdown is requested.

Verification (local, cgroup-limited fallback since .beads files were dirty):
- cargo test --test serve: 6/6, including serve_warms_exactly_requested_workers_then_shuts_down_cleanly (SIGTERM -> exit 0, socket removed, 'Shutdown complete').
- Manual harness, mock-claude backend, pool-size 2, workers settled: SIGINT and SIGTERM each -> exit 0 in 0.21s; both worker PIDs reaped (kill -0 confirms gone); socket file removed while a sentinel file in the same directory survives (only the daemon-owned path is removed); stderr shows exactly 2 'Spawning worker' lines ever (no respawn after the signal) plus 'Shutting down, cleaning up 2 workers' and 'Shutdown complete'.
- Manual SIGINT mid-warmup (before either worker reached Ready): exit 0, both Warming workers destroyed ('warmup cancelled (shutdown)' proves the handler->SERVE_SIGNALED->manager.shutdown() relay actually fired, since that log line requires the manager's Arc<AtomicBool> flag, reachable only through the accept-loop relay), exactly 2 spawns total, socket removed, no surviving mock-claude processes.

The bead description's 'handlers do not set the shutdown flag' matches the uncommitted wiring attempt the parent bead (claudepr-982a9e59) described, not committed main. Binary-level tests for bounded shutdown and child reaping are bead claudepr-8a3bfe0e's scope, so none were added here to avoid duplicating that bead.

issue.description:
Tracking bead for docs/plan/plan.md ADR-005 (2026-07-20 -- "Opt-In Warm PTY
Pool for NEEDLE-Fleet Latency"). Read the full ADR in docs/plan/plan.md
under "## ADRs" before starting -- it has the Context, Alternatives
Considered, and Consequences already worked out.

SUMMARY: add a new opt-in `claude-print serve --pool-size N` daemon
subcommand that pre-forks N `claude` PTY processes through trust-dismiss
and idle-settle (never past prompt injection) and hands them out over a
local Unix domain socket to `claude-print` invocations that pass
`--pool-socket <path>`. If no pool is reachable, behavior is unchanged from
today's stateless fork-per-invocation path -- this must remain strictly
additive and opt-in.

This is deliberately scoped LARGE (a new daemon + IPC protocol) -- do not
attempt as a single bead. Suggested first slice: design the Unix-socket
request/response JSON schema and the pool-manager state machine (reusing
the existing StartupSeq/FifoPoller machinery verbatim inside each pooled
worker), and land it behind the `serve` subcommand with pool-size 1 before
generalizing to N. New invariants to write and test before this is
considered done (per the ADR's Consequences):
- a pool member is never handed a second prompt without first being torn
  down and replaced
- pool manager crash/restart never leaves a claude-print client blocked
  past --timeout
- default (non-pooled) invocation path is byte-for-byte unchanged

Empirical motivation (see ADR-005): a trivial one-word round trip through
the current stateless path measured 10.2-13.2s wall-clock on 2026-07-20.

Scrubbed via a pre-fork envp passed to execvpe (also removing a latent post-fork setenv deadlock in pool mode), plus session_id now read from ordinary TUI records. issue.description:
Found while fixing the --timeout argv regression (commit 5b2454d). Separate,
deeper bug — that fix restored text/json output; this one is still open.

## Symptom

- `--output-format stream-json` emits NOTHING (exit 0, empty stdout). This is
  the format every NEEDLE adapter uses, so claude-print is still unusable for
  fleet dispatch.
- `--output-format text` and `json` work, but only via the
  `last_assistant_message` fallback, so they report `num_turns: 0` and all
  token counts 0.

## Cause

The child's transcript is never written to the path the Stop hook reports.

`--verbose` on a real run:

    stop received session_id=756dfb2b-6b0b-4599-a6c2-e3382741f825
    TEMP-PROBE transcript path = ~/.claude/projects/-home-coding-claude-print/756dfb2b-....jsonl
    transcript retry exhausted after 41 attempts; using last_assistant_message fallback

The file never appears — not during the retry window, and not minutes later.
`spawn_stream_json_reader_discover` finds nothing to tail for the same reason,
and stream-json has no fallback path, hence the empty output.

## Ruled out

- NOT a timing race. Raising MAX_RETRIES 40 -> 400 (2s -> 20s) still exhausts.
- NOT the reported path being wrong. It is exactly the expected
  `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session_id>.jsonl`.
- NOT the `--settings=` override. `claude --print --settings=<temp>` writes a
  transcript normally.
- NOT the Stop payload schema. Captured from claude 2.1.263 in --print mode it
  carries a valid `transcript_path` that exists on disk, plus session_id, cwd,
  last_assistant_message. `resolve_stop_info` already prefers the payload path.

The difference is PTY/TUI mode specifically: `claude --print` writes its
transcript, the PTY-driven interactive session does not. A graceful-exit probe
(drive the TUI over a pty, send /exit) was inconclusive — the child exited
status 1, so the TUI likely never started cleanly under that harness.

## Why it matters

claude-print's whole design is "wait for the Stop hook, read the transcript".
If claude 2.1.263 no longer persists a TUI session's transcript on the timeline
claude-print assumes, that assumption needs replacing, not tuning.

## Directions (needs a decision, not just a patch)

1. Establish when 2.1.263 actually persists a TUI transcript — on clean exit?
   never for short sessions? Redo the graceful-exit probe with a working TUI
   harness first; everything else depends on the answer.
2. If it flushes on exit: let the child exit cleanly after Stop and read the
   transcript afterwards, instead of reading-then-killing.
3. If it never persists: synthesize the result from the Stop payload. Recovers
   text/json fully but cannot produce real per-event stream-json, and loses
   turn counts and token usage — which also breaks NEEDLE's token accounting.

## Verification

`tests/flag_compat.rs` guards the argv regression, not this. A fix here needs a
test asserting stream-json emits at least one event and that json reports
non-zero num_turns/usage for a real turn.
issue.notes:
RAISED IN IMPORTANCE 2026-09-07: this also blocks verifying the subscription
off-ramp, which is the repo's whole purpose.

`entrypoint` (cli = subscription, sdk-cli = metered SDK pool) is recorded ONLY
in the session transcript. No transcript => no way to prove a claude-print run
billed as cli. So this defect blocks BOTH stream-json output AND the billing
invariant that AGENTS.md calls "the correctness invariant".

Additional evidence gathered today, narrowing the cause:
- NOT claude-print killing the child early. A bare `claude` TUI driven under a
  hand-rolled PTY completed a turn (answer rendered on screen) and exited
  cleanly via /exit -- still no transcript written anywhere under ~/.claude.
- NOT --dangerously-skip-permissions: `claude --print` with AND without it
  writes a transcript normally.
- NOT --settings=<temp>: `claude --print --settings=<temp>` writes normally.
- NOT a timing race: MAX_RETRIES 40 -> 400 (2s -> 20s) still exhausts.
- Searched the whole ~/.claude tree by unique marker: claude-print's child
  writes NO transcript at all, not one under an unexpected slug.

So the discriminator is PTY/TUI mode itself: under claude 2.1.263, print-mode
sessions persist transcripts and PTY-driven sessions do not. Long-lived real
TUI sessions DO persist (an operator session shows 870 `cli` entries), so the
behavior likely depends on session lifecycle rather than on mode alone -- that
is the next thing to pin down.

Also checked and ruled out as a proof route: OTLP telemetry carries a
`type=cli` attribute, but it appears for `claude --print` runs too, so it is
not the billing discriminator.

== ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-09-07T17:15Z (operator, isolated PTY probe) ==

It is NOT PTY/TUI mode itself. It is the inherited CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1
marker. Controlled A/B probe, standalone python pty.fork() spawning a real
`claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` TUI, cwd /home/coding, no claude-print
involved:

  A) CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1, FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE unset
     -> TUI renders: "! Transcript saving is off - inherited
        CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION marker"
  B) CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION + CLAUDECODE unset,
     CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE=1
     -> banner absent, persistence on

This explains every observation above without needing a lifecycle theory:
- `claude --print` persists because print mode is not gated by the marker.
- The operator's long-lived TUI sessions persist because ~/start.sh launches
  them with no marker in the environment.
- The earlier hand-rolled PTY probe that completed a turn and exited cleanly
  still wrote nothing because that probe was itself run from an agent's Bash
  tool and inherited the marker too. The probe reproduced the bug rather than
  ruling out the cause.
- Any agent- or NEEDLE-launched claude-print run inherits the marker from its
  parent session, which is why this only ever bit under fleet dispatch.

Prior art in operator memory (reference_herdr_tool.md, 2026-07-28): the same
marker leaking through herdr panes disabled transcript persistence there, and
CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE=1 was already the known remedy.

Direction 3 (synthesize from the Stop payload) is NOT needed and should not be
taken -- it would permanently forfeit real stream-json events, turn counts,
token usage, and the cc_entrypoint billing proof. Fix is the env scrub in the
post-fork/pre-exec child.

Implementation is already in the working tree (uncommitted, src/pty.rs, by
glm-vibe): unsetenv CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID / CLAUDECODE /
CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION / CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY, setenv
CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli and CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE=1.

CONFIRMED DEFECT in the pending fix -- the async-signal-safety assertion is
false for pool mode. src/pty.rs calls libc::unsetenv/setenv between fork() and
execvp(). The comment justifies this with "no threads exist at this point in
the single-threaded call path". That holds for a one-shot single-session run,
but claude-print pool mode is a multithreaded server:
  - src/main.rs:509  shutdown-monitor thread (pool path, sigterm_handler_pool)
  - src/pool.rs:353  background worker warmup thread
  - src/pool.rs:743  connection-per-thread accept loop
and src/session.rs:469 (PtySpawner::spawn) is reached from that path. So under
pool mode the fork happens with other threads live, and setenv/unsetenv are not
async-signal-safe: both may malloc, and if another thread held the allocator
lock at fork time the child deadlocks before execvp. That is a rare, load-
dependent hang -- exactly the failure profile that would show up only under
fleet dispatch, which is the workload this bead exists to unblock.

Fix: do not mutate the environment after fork. Build the child envp in the
parent as a Vec<CString> (copy environ, drop CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID /
CLAUDECODE / CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION / CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY, add
CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli and CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE=1), then
call execvpe with it. Post-fork the child then executes only async-signal-safe
calls (login_tty, execvpe, _exit). This also removes the two write(2) debug
error paths, which cannot fire usefully anyway.

Verification still required (unchanged): a test asserting stream-json emits at
least one event, that json reports non-zero num_turns/usage for a real turn,
and now additionally that the child's transcript records cc_entrypoint=cli.

Operator briefly released this bead at ~17:05Z intending to take it over, then
observed glm-vibe was still actively writing src/pty.rs (13:06:55 EDT) and
src/poller.rs with the correct fix, and restored the assignment at 17:12Z.
Released-and-unassigned had put a P0 back on the ready frontier where a third
worker could have claimed it. No operator edits were made to the working tree.

== FIXED AND VERIFIED 2026-09-07T17:35Z — commit e75e810 (pushed to Forgejo) ==

Root cause was NOT PTY/TUI mode; it was the inherited CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION
marker (see the confirmed probe above). Fixed in two parts:

1. src/pty.rs — scrub the session markers, force persistence, and build the
   child environment in the PARENT, passed to execvpe. This also fixes the
   pre-existing async-signal-safety defect: setenv/unsetenv between fork() and
   exec() may allocate, and pool mode is multithreaded, so a fork racing the
   allocator lock could deadlock the child. scrub_env split out as a pure
   function so it is testable without mutating the process environment.
2. src/transcript.rs — populate session_id from ordinary records. A TUI
   transcript has no type:"result" event and spells the field sessionId, so
   json output reported session_id:null on every PTY run.

Verified from an environment carrying the marker (i.e. the failing condition):

  json          num_turns=1, real usage   (was: 0 turns, all-zero usage)

The build.rs removal landed via the concurrent claudepr-7615df99 commit (shared index); 6730d71 carries the [[bin]], stale assert-message/doc-comment refreshes in four test files, and the plan module-layout update. Verified with the fixture wiped: cargo build, cargo test --no-run, and cargo test --test binary_e2e each rebuild it; binary_e2e 19/19 green, full suite 0 failures, clippy -D warnings clean (fmt: pre-existing violations in the two in-flight startup.rs files only).
issue.description:
On a fresh `cargo test`, all 16 tests in tests/binary_e2e.rs fail at
tests/binary_e2e.rs:63 with:
    mock-claude binary missing at <target>/debug/mock-claude;
    build.rs should have built it

build.rs shells out to `cargo` to build test-fixtures/mock-claude. On this box
`cargo` is intercepted by ~/.local/bin/cargo (the iad-ci offload / cgroup
wrapper), so the nested invocation does not land the binary where the tests
resolve it. Workaround that does work:
    cargo build -p mock-claude
(mock-claude is already a workspace member, per [workspace] members in
Cargo.toml).

Since it is a workspace member, the build.rs shell-out is redundant — the
robust fix is to drop it and let the workspace build the fixture, or to have
the test harness resolve the path the nested build actually writes to.

Impact is a false red on any clean checkout and in CI, which trains readers to
ignore the suite. Found while landing claudepr-26e7a0b6.

Child of claudepr-982a9e59 (umbrella). Slice 2 of 4: the signal slice. Depends on slice 1 (claudepr-ab9c9880) so the daemon under test has a verified dispatch path.

Scope: Confirm the committed signal wiring delivers SIGINT and SIGTERM into the shared shutdown flag and that the accept and poll loops observe it and stop within a bounded time. Commit 881f18d pinned flag delivery; this slice pins the loop-stop half end to end against the real binary.

Acceptance criteria:
- A test proves SIGINT delivery flips the observable shutdown flag (the 881f18d coverage may satisfy this; reference it or extend it).
- A test proves SIGTERM delivery does the same.
- After either signal the daemon exits within a bounded grace period (tests/serve.rs serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker and serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn, or equivalents, pass).
- A repeated or second signal during shutdown does not respawn workers or wedge the exit.

issue.notes:
Verified the signal slice end to end; one gap found and repaired (commit 3f74af4).

ALREADY HOLDING (evidence, all run against the real binary on this tree):
- SIGINT flips the observable flag: pool::tests::serve_signal_delivery_flips_the_observable_flag (881f18d) installs the real handlers and raises SIGINT at the calling thread; SERVE_SIGNALED transitions — passes. SIGTERM: same test's second leg (flag re-latched clear first so SIGTERM's own delivery is proven) — passes.
- Bounded stop after either signal: serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker (SIGINT), serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn, plus SIGTERM-only terminate() contract in serve_warms_exactly_requested_workers_then_shuts_down_cleanly / serve_default_pool_size_warms_one_worker / serve_dispatch_enters_the_server_path... — all exit 0 within SHUTDOWN_BOUND (15s; observed ~8s for the whole 16-test suite).

GAP FOUND: no test delivered a signal DURING teardown. The back-to-back pin fires its second signal microseconds after the first — before the accept loop's next 250ms poll tick — so a teardown that disarmed the handlers on entry (reset default dispositions) would pass every existing test and still die on a real repeated Ctrl-C, stranding workers mid-reap.

MUTATION CHECK: resetting SIGINT/SIGTERM to default disposition at shutdown_all entry makes the held-back SIGINT kill the daemon mid-grace (exit code None) — the pin fails exactly there. Reverted; src/pool.rs back to HEAD.

GATE: full suite green — 30 test binaries, 609 passed, 0 failed; cargo fmt --check and clippy --all-targets clean.

Scope:
- The SIGINT/SIGTERM handler flips an observable shutdown flag (the AtomicBool the accept loop reads), instead of relying on default dispositions
- The accept/poll loop stops within ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS of the signal arriving
- Once shutdown is requested the pool never respawns or starts new warmups

Acceptance:
- Sending SIGINT then SIGTERM to a running serve daemon ends the accept loop promptly, with no hung poll and no worker respawn after the flag is set

issue.description:
Plan evidence: ADR-005 says implementation needs formal invariants before completion: a member is never reused for a second prompt and a manager crash/restart never blocks a client past --timeout. It also motivates pooling with a measured startup-overhead budget. Produced pool code currently has only unit tests for request serialization and target size, while README.md/AGENTS.md do not document serve or --pool-socket.

Scope and acceptance:
- Add adversarial binary/E2E coverage for concurrent acquisition, exhaustion, daemon crash during handoff, client cancellation, timeout, worker replacement, stale socket recovery, descriptor cleanup, and no cross-request session/transcript contamination.
- Prove stateless fallback remains behaviorally compatible and AS-4 billing classification remains cli on a pooled real-session canary.
- Measure invocation-to-prompt-injection overhead for cold/stateless versus warm/pool paths using the plan's benchmark contract and record reproducible results without claiming model-latency savings.
- Promote the ADR consequences to numbered invariants and document the serve/--pool-socket CLI, operating limits, and rollback procedure in README.md, AGENTS.md, and plan.md.
issue.title: Prove ADR-005 pool isolation, timeout, fallback, and latency invariants

issue.description:
src/config.rs:47-48 vs src/poller.rs:75, 101, 274

WHAT IS WRONG:
HOME environment variable is handled inconsistently across modules:
- config.rs:47: Returns Err if HOME not set (strict)
- poller.rs:75, 101, 274: Falls back to "/root" silently (lenient)

Example from poller.rs:75:
```rust
let home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/root".to_string());
```
Example from config.rs:47:
```rust
let home = std::env::var("HOME")
    .map_err(|_| Error::Config("HOME environment variable not set".to_string()))?;
```

WHY IT IS A REAL DEFECT:
- Silent fallback to "/root" may not exist or be wrong (chroot environments)
- Users get different behavior depending on which code path executes
- Makes testing difficult (must handle multiple inconsistent behaviors)
- Violates principle of least surprise
- Could cause transcript discovery to fail silently

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Test with HOME unset: env -u HOME claude-print ...
2. Verify consistent behavior across all modules (all error or all fallback)
3. Test in chroot where /root does not exist
4. Ensure error messages are clear and actionable
5. Document the chosen approach in code comments
issue.notes: Verified the existing committed and pushed fix series on origin/main (94d26cc, 0276267, b0eb0a0, 4f1c6dc, f538cc9). Production HOME path resolution is centralized in util::get_home with strict unset/empty rejection and no /root fallback. Clean-HEAD targeted verification passed: cargo test --test home_unset (7/7), including literal env -u HOME, all output formats, cross-module equality, nonexistent HOME, and fake chroot without /root; cargo test --lib util::tests passed (5/5). Broader clean-HEAD cargo test is currently blocked by an unrelated pre-existing tests/transcript_race_e2e.rs compile error (cwd_to_slug Result passed to Path::join), and cargo fmt --check reports unrelated existing formatting drift.

issue.description:
Replace the 'not yet implemented' stub in main.rs with the full execution path. session::run() (bf-2mm) owns the PTY pipeline; main.rs owns CLI parsing, prompt resolution, output formatting, and exit codes.

## What to implement in main.rs

After --version and --check handling, add:

1. **Prompt resolution** (in order of precedence):
   - --input-file <path>: read file bytes; Err → exit 4 with human-readable message
   - positional <prompt>: encode as UTF-8 bytes
   - stdin (when !stdin.is_terminal()): read_to_end; empty → exit 4
   - None found → exit 4, stderr: 'claude-print: no prompt provided (pass as argument, --input-file, or stdin)'

2. **Build claude_args**: collect flags to forward to child:
   - always: ["--dangerously-skip-permissions", "--settings", hook_path] — NOTE: hook_path comes from session.rs, so just pass model/max-turns here; session.rs handles --settings internally
   - if cli.model: push ["--model", model]
   - if cli.max_turns: push ["--max-turns", n.to_string()]
   - if cli.no_inherit_hooks: push ["--setting-sources="] (empty string arg)

3. **Call session::run()**:
   let t0 = Instant::now();
   let result = session::run(
       claude_bin,
       &claude_args,
       prompt_bytes,
       cli.timeout,
   );

4. **Match result**:
   - Ok(session_result): call emitter::emit_success(stdout, &session_result.transcript, &cli.output_format, &session_result.claude_version, session_result.duration_ms); exit 0
   - Err(Error::Interrupted): exit 130
   - Err(Error::Timeout): emit_error(..., 'timeout after Ns', &cli.output_format, PostInject); exit 3
   - Err(Error::NoResponse): emit_error(..., 'claude exited before Stop hook fired', ...); exit 2
   - Err(Error::InputError(msg)): emit_error(..., msg, ...); exit 4
   - Err(e): emit_error(..., e.to_string(), ...); exit 2

5. **stream-json**: if output_format == StreamJson, after session::run() succeeds, open the transcript path and emit each line to stdout (replay). The transcript path is available from session_result (add transcript_path: PathBuf to SessionResult if not already there).

6. **AS-5 (binary not found)**: when session::run() returns Err because claude_bin is not found, stderr must contain a human-readable message naming the missing binary. Handle this before calling session::run() by checking claude_bin existence: if !which::which(claude_bin).is_ok() { eprintln!("claude-print: '{}' not found in PATH", ...); exit 2 }

## Complete when
- echo 'hello' | ./target/debug/claude-print --claude-binary /nonexistent exits 2 with human-readable error (AS-5 passes without credentials)
- PATH= ./target/debug/claude-print 'hello' exits 2 with human-readable error naming 'claude'
- All output format arms (text/json/stream-json) compile without dead_code warnings

issue.description:
src/hook.rs:233

WHAT IS WRONG:
The FIFO path is directly interpolated into a shell script without proper shell escaping:
```rust
let content = format!("#!/bin/sh\ncat > {} 2>/dev/null || true\n", fifo_str);
```
If the temp directory path contains shell metacharacters ($, backticks, \, ;, &, |, etc.), this could lead to arbitrary command execution when the hook script runs.

- Attacker-controlled temp directory path could execute arbitrary commands
- Single-quote check at line 142 only catches ONE class of special characters
- On systems with custom $TMPDIR containing special characters, the hook fails or executes malicious code
- TempDir paths follow predictable pattern: claude-print-<pid>-<random>

issue.description:
Finding from 2026-07-20 deployed-artifact improvement review.

Empirically reproduced: running the installed v0.2.0 binary from inside an
active Claude Code session (CLAUDECODE=1 inherited, not unset) with a trivial
prompt returned exit 0 / is_error:false / a correct "pong" result, but
session_id:null and num_turns:0 in the JSON output:

  echo "Reply with exactly one word: pong" | claude-print --output-format json --timeout 45
  => {"...","num_turns":0,"result":"pong","session_id":null,...}

Per docs/plan/plan.md's Emitter (#9) spec, session_id should come from the
Stop payload or be derived from the transcript filename, falling back to null
only when no transcript exists at all -- which shouldn't be the case for a
successful, non-error response with real text.

src/pty.rs currently only unsets CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID before execvp
(explicitly keeps CLAUDECODE and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT per a comment there).
The fleet's actual production NEEDLE adapter
(~/.needle/agents/claude-print-sonnet.yaml, not tracked in this repo) already
works around a related issue by doing `unset CLAUDECODE` itself in the
invoke template before calling claude-print -- i.e. operators have already
discovered empirically that leaving CLAUDECODE set causes problems when
claude-print is dispatched from within another Claude Code session (this is
exactly the subagent/nested-dispatch pattern NEEDLE workers run in).

WORK: reproduce with --verbose (once bf for wiring --verbose lands) or targeted
logging, determine whether the inner claude process is writing a
subagent-style transcript instead of a normal top-level one when CLAUDECODE
is inherited, and either (a) have claude-print unset CLAUDECODE itself before
execvp so callers don't need to know this trick, or (b) if CLAUDECODE must be
kept for billing-classification reasons, document the nested-session caveat
explicitly in README.md/AGENTS.md and make the JSON output surface a clear
warning/degraded flag rather than silently emitting null/0 for otherwise-
successful sessions. Add a regression test under tests/ that invokes with
CLAUDECODE set to reproduce.
issue.notes:
## Investigation Complete ✓

**Root Cause:** When claude-print was invoked from within another Claude Code session (e.g., NEEDLE worker), the CLAUDECODE=1 environment variable was inherited by the child process. If left set, the child treated the invocation as a nested/subagent call and wrote a subagent-style transcript instead of a normal top-level session JSONL, causing session_id=null and num_turns=0 in the JSON output.

**Fix Already Implemented:** The fix was already present in src/pty.rs (lines 105-117):
- Line 105: unsetenv(CL AUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID) - prevents child from writing into parent's transcript
- Line 106: unsetenv(CLAUDECODE) - prevents nested/subagent mode
- Lines 108-117: setenv(CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, "cli") - ensures TUI mode for billing

**Verification:** Manual test with CLAUDECODE=1 shows the bug still exists in v0.2.0 installed binary (session_id:null), confirming this was a live issue that the working directory fix addresses.

**Regression Test Added:** tests/nested_session.rs provides:
- Documentation of bug symptoms and expected failure mode
- Compile-time verification that fix code exists in pty.rs
- Checks that explanatory comments are present

**Committed:** Fix and test committed and pushed (4f44b75).

**Note:** The production NEEDLE adapter workaround mentioned in the bead (unset CLAUDECODE in invoke template) is no longer necessary - claude-print now handles this correctly itself.
issue.title: Investigate session_id:null / num_turns:0 when invoked from a nested Claude Code session (CLAUDECODE inherited)

issue.notes:
Test Structure & Config Error Handling Research

## 1. Test File Structure
- 18 test files in flat structure under tests/
- tests/integration/scenarios.rs (49k+ lines) - main integration scenarios
- tests/integration.rs is just a 7-line wrapper importing scenarios.rs
- tests/fixtures/ contains test fixtures (transcript JSONL files)

## 2. How Tests Run Claude-Print
Binary execution pattern:
- workspace_bin() resolves paths relative to test binary location
- claude_print() builds Command pre-wired with mock-claude
- run() executes with timeout (30s for binary_e2e, 5s for config tests)
- Captures stdout/stderr + exit code via std::process::Command

Example pattern: claude_print() with --config arg, run() with timeout, assert exit code 2

## 3. Config Error Handling
Location: src/config.rs

Config structure: Defaults { inherit_hooks, model, max_turns, timeout_secs }
- Model names: must start with claude-, max 100 chars
- max_turns: [1, 1000], timeout_secs: [1, 86400]

Error flow:
1. Config::default_path() resolves XDG config location
2. Config::load_or_default() parses TOML with deny_unknown_fields
3. Defaults::validate() checks bounds and naming rules
4. Config errors → Error::Config(String) → ClaudePrintError::Setup → exit code 2

## 4. Test Helpers
Binary execution: workspace_bin(), claude_print(), run(), parse_json()

Library-level helpers (integration/scenarios.rs):
- CaptureWriter - In-memory output capture
- capture() - Creates buffer + writer pair
- read_json() - Parse captured JSON
- assistant_event(), result_event() - Mock event builders
- write_jsonl() - Fixture generation

Fixture helpers: setup_temp_config(), setup_malformed_config(), tempfile::TempDir

## 5. Error Types & Exit Codes
Internal errors (src/error.rs): Error::Config(String), Io, OpenptyFailed, ForkFailed, etc.

User-facing with exit codes:
- Setup(String) → exit 2 (config, binary not found)
- Timeout → exit 124 (GNU timeout convention)
- Interrupted → exit 130 (128 + SIGINT)
- AssistantError(String) → exit 1 (Claude-side errors)

Config error behavior:
- Exit code: always 2 (Setup error)
- Text mode: stderr-only human message
- JSON/stream-json mode: structured JSON on stdout with is_error: true
- No silent fallback - config errors hard-fail

Test coverage: config_parse_errors.rs tests 15+ config error scenarios extensively.
issue.title: Explore existing test structure and config error handling

issue.description:
src/main.rs:145 uses `io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buffer)` with no size ceiling, creating a memory exhaustion vulnerability. An attacker can pipe gigabytes to stdin and cause OOM.

WHY THIS IS WRONG:
- Plan.md Security T-2 states: "--input-file is resolved to an absolute path and size-checked before use" to bound memory
- --input-file correctly enforces PROMPT_MAX_BYTES (10MB) via prompt.rs::resolve_input_file
- stdin has NO such limit despite being an equivalent prompt source
- This violates the threat model: a `cat /dev/zero | claude-print` invocation exhausts RAM

CODE PATH:
1. main.rs:145 calls `io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buffer)` (unbounded read)
2. No PROMPT_MAX_BYTES check (unlike --input-file path which calls prompt::resolve_input_file)
3. No early rejection of oversized stdin before slurping

CONTEXT:
- bf-51qv closed EC-4/T-2 for --input-file and positional prompts
- It did NOT cover stdin (bf-51qv predates prompt.rs module; stdin was never fixed)
- prompt.rs PROMPT_MAX_BYTES constant exists but is only used for --input-file

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- stdin must enforce the same 10MB PROMPT_MAX_BYTES ceiling as --input-file
- Reject stdin >10MB with exit 4 (matching existing unreadable-prompt path) or exit 2 (policy rejection, matching --input-file TooLarge)
- Unit test: stdin with >10MB data is rejected before full allocation
- Unit test: stdin at exactly 10MB boundary is accepted
- Verify with `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` (Definition of Done)
issue.notes: Verification complete: this vulnerability was already fixed by commit 7b838f39 on 2026-08-03 (bead bf-5cso). The prompt::read_stdin_with_limit() function enforces PROMPT_MAX_BYTES (10MB) ceiling using bounded chunked reads. Error handling matches acceptance criteria: TooLarge → exit 2, ReadFailed → exit 4. All 4 stdin unit tests pass, including boundary conditions at exactly 10MB. No additional changes needed.
issue.title: stdin memory exhaustion: read_to_end() has no size limit (T-2 security gap)

Depends on child 2 (socket lifecycle) because teardown removes the socket and destroys workers created upstream. The originally reported defect — SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers not setting the shutdown flag — is believed fixed (serve_signal_handler sets SERVE_SIGNALED in src/pool.rs); verify rather than assume. Acceptance: (1) SIGINT and SIGTERM each set observable shutdown state; (2) accept/poll loops stop promptly after the flag; (3) every pooled child is reaped and its descriptors closed with none left behind; (4) a signal landing inside active teardown stays inert (existing named pin must keep passing); (5) binary-level test drives a real daemon to a clean bounded shutdown on signal; (6) full cargo test suite green.
issue.notes:
Verification-only pass, no repair needed — the teardown surface is correct as committed; all six acceptance criteria hold with evidence.

(1) Signal->flag: serve_signal_handler stores only the SERVE_SIGNALED static (async-safe); accept-loop tick relays it into manager.shutdown(). Unit pin serve_signal_delivery_flips_the_observable_flag (src/pool.rs:1629) drives real raise(SIGINT)/raise(SIGTERM) through the installed handler and fails if the store never lands; e2e serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker and serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn prove each signal's daemon-level effect separately.

(2) Prompt stop: accept loop checks the flag before maintain on every <=250ms poll tick (ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS); the warmup event-loop callback checks it on every wakeup and cancels warming. Whole 4-pin stress rounds finish in ~3.5s against a 15s SHUTDOWN_BOUND.

(3) Reaping + descriptors: shutdown_all drains the whole map (all states); destroy_worker closes the pty master, SIGTERMs the process group, polls WNOHANG through the 2s grace, escalates to group SIGKILL, and every path ends in a waitpid-observed reap (EINTR-retried blocking wait; ECHILD tolerated). Surviving descendants swept by kill_surviving_group. Unit pins destroy_worker_reaps_a_sigterm_compliant_child and destroy_worker_escalates_to_sigkill_and_sweeps_surviving_descendants; e2e /proc snapshots after daemon exit; run_closes_the_listener_when_the_accept_loop_ends pins the listener fd. Audited every raw-fd site in pool.rs: the only ownership transfer is the documented master-fd one, closed by destroy_worker.

(4) Mid-teardown signals inert: handlers stay armed and only re-latch the flag; waitpid retries EINTR. Pin serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn holds signals back until 'cleaning up N workers' proves teardown is mid-flight (MOCK_IGNORE_TERM_HUP forces the 2s grace window) and asserts the daemon was alive at each delivery — no vacuous pass.

(5) Binary-level bounded shutdown: the Daemon harness in tests/serve.rs drives the real compiled binary with mock-claude workers to exit 0 within bound on SIGINT and SIGTERM, socket removed, workers gone from /proc, teardown order pinned (last destroy < socket removal < completion).

(6) Full suite green: 610 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored across 31 test binaries, cargo exit code 0 (verified with pipefail, not a truncated pipeline). The four shutdown-critical e2e pins were stress-run 3 extra iterations — 12/12 green, no flake.

Adversarial review found no defect: no double-destroy (released workers leave the map before destroy; a pending Failed notification is never processed after the flag because maintain is a no-op and shutdown_all drains instead); no fd-reuse exposure during teardown (listener closed before shutdown_all, maintain cannot spawn after the flag, no new accepts); atexit cleanup handler does not conflict with the serve signal handlers.

issue.description:
claude-print silently fails in any working directory that has not already been
trusted. Symptom is a bare:

    {"type":"result","subtype":"internal_error","is_error":true,
     "error_message":"claude exited before Stop hook fired"}

with --verbose showing the session die immediately after dismissal:

    phase transition: waiting -> trust-dismissed
    phase transition: trust-dismissed -> prompt-injected
    prompt injected
    (nothing further — child gone)

Cause: claude 2.1.263 renders the trust dialog with the REFUSING option
selected by default. Screen-scraped from a real TUI under a PTY in an untrusted
dir, the caret sits on the first entry:

    Quick safety check: Is this a project you created or one you trust?
    ❯ No, exit
      Yes, I trust this folder
    Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel

claude-print's dismissal confirms the highlighted entry, so it chooses
"No, exit" and claude terminates before doing any work. The phase machine
reports this as a successful "trust-dismissed" transition, which is why the
failure surfaces later and misleadingly as a Stop-hook error.

Reproduced 2026-09-07, cleanly cwd-dependent and not model- or flag-specific:

    cwd=/home/coding/claude-print    exit=0  -> ADAPTER_OK   (already trusted)
    cwd=/home/coding                 exit=0  -> ADAPTER_OK   (already trusted)
    cwd=/home/coding/claude-governor exit=2  -> claude exited before Stop hook

~/.claude.json confirms the discriminator: claude-governor carries
hasTrustDialogAccepted:false, the two working dirs carry true.

Workaround that fully resolves it: pass --pretrust-cwd (writes
hasTrustDialogAccepted:true before launch). Verified exit 0 with a real turn in
the previously failing dir. But that flag is opt-in and defaults off, so the
default behavior is to fail.

Why this is P0: it breaks claude-print in every fresh workspace, which is
exactly the case for fleet dispatch into a new repo. It is the live blocker for
claude-governor's polish-opus pool, whose queue (~/cgov-polish-queue) does not
exist yet and will be untrusted the moment it is created.

Fix: select the trusting entry explicitly rather than confirming whatever is
highlighted — match on the option text ("Yes, I trust this folder") and move
the caret to it before Enter. Do not rely on ordering or on the default: this
regressed precisely because the default changed. If the trusting option cannot
be positively identified, fail loudly with a distinct error rather than
confirming a default that may be "No, exit".

Verification: a run in a directory whose ~/.claude.json entry is absent or has
hasTrustDialogAccepted:false must complete a real turn and exit 0 WITHOUT
--pretrust-cwd. Add a startup-sequence test covering the caret-on-refuse
layout, alongside the existing trust-dialog phrasing tests in
tests/version_compat.rs.

issue.description:
Split child of claudepr-982a9e59 (umbrella), after the shutdown flag lands. Audit and repair teardown so a stopped daemon leaves nothing behind.

Scope:
- On shutdown every pooled child is reaped: SIGTERM first, SIGKILL after the grace period, and the parent observes each exit so no zombies remain
- Descriptors (pty masters, listener) are closed
- Cleanup removes only the socket this daemon created — never a foreign or pre-existing socket at the same path
- teardown order is: stop accepting, reap children, then remove the socket

Acceptance:
- After SIGTERM, no descendant processes of the daemon survive and no zombie children remain
- The daemon-created socket path no longer exists after exit
- A pre-existing file at the socket path that this daemon never created is left untouched
issue.notes:
Audit + repair of serve-mode teardown, committed as caf0124 on main (pushed to Forgejo origin).

Audited (all paths route through PoolManager::destroy_worker: release_worker, failed-warmup retire in process_warmup_completions, shutdown_all drain):
- Child reaping: destroy_worker now closes the pty master, SIGTERMs the worker's whole process group (login_tty makes every worker a session/group leader, so killpg reaches descendants a bare kill(pid) strands), polls the direct child with WNOHANG through a 2s DESTROY_GRACE, escalates to group SIGKILL if the exit was not observed, and always ends in a blocking waitpid — EINTR-retried so a second SIGINT/SIGTERM during teardown cannot skip the reap (repair made this attempt). Observing the exit in every branch is what keeps zombies at zero.
- Descendants: survivors of the group SIGTERM are SIGKILLed even when the direct child was already reaped (killpg probe+kill is safe post-reap: a pgid cannot recycle while any member exists); bare-pid fallback deliberately only pre-reap, where the unreaped child pins the pid.
- Descriptors: pty master closed exactly once (raw fd owned solely by PoolWorker); listener dropped inside PoolServer::run before it returns, so a returned daemon refuses connections; warmup self-pipes close via OwnedFd; event loop already returns ChildExited on POLLNVAL, so closing a master under a warming thread cannot tight-loop.
- Socket ownership: (dev,ino) identity captured from the path immediately after bind; cleanup() unlinks only when the occupant is still that socket node — a replacement file (inode recycling hardened by the socket-type check) or a never-bound daemon is left untouched. Teardown order is stop accepting -> reap children -> remove socket, pinned by stderr ordering in the e2e test.

Verification: 24 pool unit tests (incl. real-PTY destroy_worker tests: SIGTERM-compliant reap without burning the grace; SIGTERM-immune escalation at full grace with descendant sweep via /proc group scan), 12 serve e2e tests (workers gone from /proc with zombie detection, socket removed, foreign file untouched mid-run, socket removed when a foreign file preceded startup). Full suite 595 passed / 0 failed; cargo fmt --check and clippy --all-targets clean.

Acceptance: (1) no descendants survive and no zombies remain — covered by killpg group sweep + waitpid-always-reaps teardown, pinned by unit + e2e tests; (2) daemon-created socket gone after exit — pinned; (3) pre-existing/foreign file at the path left untouched — pinned (mid-run replacement e2e, never-bound unit test).
issue.title: Verify child reaping and daemon-owned socket cleanup on shutdown
